title.narrative: Rehabilitation of the "Trucks" water desalination plant and construction of a new desalination plant at the Children's Hospital

description.narrative: - Operating the two desalination plants and providing a large percentage and achieving high sufficiency of potable water and using medical institutions in Port Sudan. - Reducing the number of people who get sick due to drinking unsuitable water. - Assisting government agencies in Sudan and the Red Sea State in solving part of their biggest problem. - Benefiting from the truck station that was secured with millions of dollars and has not been operated or utilized. - Saving great effort and suffering made by a large number of residents in a number of the city's neighborhoods who spend a lot of time and effort to obtain clean water. - Saving huge amounts of money paid by many residents of the targeted neighborhoods to obtain clean drinking water. - Raising the efficiency of technicians by receiving distinguished training in operating the two stations and managing them well.
Providing safe and clean (drinkable) water to the most needy communities

Rehabilitation of the truck desalination station in Port Sudan, which has a production capacity of (3,000) cubic meters per day, and will benefit about (50) neighborhoods and squares in Port Sudan, with a population exceeding (400,000) people approximately, and the establishment of a water desalination station in the Children's Teaching Hospital building, which provides potable water and water for use in a number of hospitals, with a production capacity of (50) cubic meters per day. The project consists of three main activities, which are: - Maintenance and rehabilitation of the truck desalination station in Port Sudan. - Operating the truck desalination station and pumping water into the public water network in the targeted neighborhoods. - Establishing a hospital water desalination station (children, accidents, psychological, chest) and operating it and pumping water according to a network that will be established linking the hospitals.
